title: Random arrangements: isotropy and robustness of the small-λ chain geometry (precommitted numerical run)

key_results.statement: T1 (separable kernel, $L=32$, all grid points as places): $N_0$ is exactly the 4-neighbour torus grid and $\max\lvert\ell_0-\rho\lVert\Delta\rVert_{1,T}\rvert=0$ with $\rho=1.0295557$, so the code check passes.
T1b (exploratory reference; isotropic kernel, $L=32$, all grid points as places): the only neighbour offsets of $N_0$ are $(\pm1,0)$ and $(0,\pm1)$, and $B_{\rm per}=1.3006$ for $r\in[8,14]$.

T2 (isotropic kernel, $p=0.1$, five realizations per size, mean and standard error): $\bar B_{64}=1.00655\pm0.00195$ and $\bar B_{128}=0.99954\pm0.00211$; the decision at $L=128$ is isotropy supported.

T3 (seed 2311, $L=128$) decision: intermediate. Taking (d) as the mean $\varrho$ for $r\in[16,32]$ relative to its value at $\varepsilon=0$: for $\varepsilon\le10^{-6}$ there are no new or long edges, 175 tie edges are broken and (d) is 1.0415; at $\varepsilon=10^{-4}$ there are 61 long edges and (d) is 1.0239; at $\varepsilon=10^{-2}$ there are 430 long edges and (d) is 0.8250.

T4 (exploratory, no decision; $L=128$, isotropic kernel, T2 places of seed 2311 shifted by uniform offsets): the norms $S(h,h)$ have spread 0.278, there are 4 long edges, the maximum degree is 7, and (d) is 0.983 times the T3 value at $\varepsilon=0$.

open_issues: Tie edges: the grid ties (67–388 per graph in T2) lie where (N1)/(N2) do not decide; their small-λ status, and hence ℓ₀ at the 4% level, depends on the tie convention or on finite-λ corrections, which are out of scope
Error estimates: for the BLAS sums in T3 and T4 the error estimates are statistical models, checked on samples, not rigorous bounds; the grid overlaps (Step 1) are rigorously bounded

Development note: a first version of the decision routine added −2S and the ε-terms before comparing; at ε=10⁻¹² the broken-tie pairs then fell below 100 times the error estimate and their status was unreliable; the routine was replaced by the split comparison (23.3) that the common setting prescribes; no parameter, seed, window or rule was changed, and all reported numbers come from the final version

consistency_checks.check: T1 (code check) passes (23.7): the neighbour graph, the weights and Dijkstra reproduce (22.25)–(22.26) with zero deviation
Symmetry of N₀: each pair's decision is computed independently from both orientations; all 19 graphs (T1, T1b, 10×T2, 6×T3, T4) have 0 asymmetric decisions
Connectivity: N₀ is connected (Step 3); all 19 graphs have exactly one component and no ϱ is infinite
